admin_api_servers_list.usage_note: List servers under the legacy /admin-api surface, with the same rich filter set (owner, project, status, power_state, hostname, elastic_ip, private_ip, vpc, zone, region, ...) the v1 admin UI itself uses. Kept alongside the current admin-v2 catalog for environments still partly on the older API; prefer the admin-v2 equivalents when both cover the same ground.

admin_api_servers_retrieve.usage_note: Full detail for one server by id -- the v1 API's actual 'server detail' GET, something admin-v2 doesn't have an equivalent for (see cmp_admin_mcp/resources.py's note that no such GET exists there). Use this first when investigating a specific server under v1. Also the way to confirm a rebuild actually finished: right after admin_api_servers_recreate, power_state here reads 'pending'; poll this on an interval until it flips to 'running' (power_state stuck at 'pending' points to a stuck/failed rebuild) rather than assuming the recreate call's 202 response means it's done. Don't confuse this with the separate `status` field on the same response (active/building/paused/...) -- power_state is the one that actually carries pending/running.

resource_spec.name: server-v1
resource_spec.description: Full server detail under the legacy v1 admin-api.

admin_api_servers_partial_update.usage_note: Partial (PATCH) update of a server's editable fields.

admin_api_servers_destroy.usage_note: Hard-delete a server (DELETE). Irreversible -- confirm the target id via admin_api_servers_retrieve first.

admin_api_servers_action_log.usage_note: Action/audit log entries for a server -- what admin operations have been performed on it and when. Check here before retrying an action to see if it already ran.

admin_api_servers_attach_eip.usage_note: Attach an existing elastic IP to a server.

admin_api_servers_attach_privateip.usage_note: Attach an existing private IP/port to a server.

admin_api_servers_attach_subnet.usage_note: Attach a subnet/network interface to a server.

admin_api_servers_attach_volume.usage_note: Attach an existing volume to a server.

admin_api_servers_change_password.usage_note: Reset a server's admin/root password. Customer-visible and immediate -- confirm the target id carefully.

admin_api_servers_console.usage_note: Open a remote console session/URL for a server -- diagnostic access, not a mutation.

admin_api_servers_console_log.usage_note: Fetch the server's console log -- often the fastest way to see a boot-time failure directly from the guest OS/hypervisor, complementing celery/server_creator application logs.

admin_api_servers_delete.usage_note: Soft/scheduled delete via POST, distinct from the hard admin_api_servers_destroy (DELETE) -- check which behavior this environment's v1 API actually implements before relying on either as 'the' delete path.

admin_api_servers_detach_eip.usage_note: Detach an elastic IP from a server.

admin_api_servers_detach_private_ip.usage_note: Detach a private IP/port from a server.

admin_api_servers_detach_volume.usage_note: Detach a volume from a server.

admin_api_servers_evacuate.usage_note: Force-evacuate a server off its current compute host (e.g. the host is down). Disruptive -- the server restarts on a different host.

admin_api_servers_live_migrate.usage_note: Live-migrate a running server to another compute host with no guest downtime, when the target host has capacity.

admin_api_servers_migrate.usage_note: Cold-migrate a server to another compute host (guest is stopped during the move) -- use live_migrate instead when avoiding downtime matters.

admin_api_servers_reboot.usage_note: Reboot a server (soft or hard, depending on the request body).

admin_api_servers_recreate.usage_note: The actual, real recreate-server endpoint on the legacy v1 admin-api (/admin-api/servers/{id}/recreate/) -- unlike admin-v2, which has no such operation (see legacy_operations.py and the rebuild_server annotation). Retry a failed server build under v1. Confirm root cause first; if it was a state-drift issue, resync that resource before retrying. Returns 202 Accepted with no completion signal -- this only starts the recreate. The server's power_state goes to 'pending' while it runs; poll admin_api_servers_retrieve every so often and watch that field (not the separate `status` field) flip to 'running' before treating the retry as successful.
preconditions: if root cause was a state-drift (volume/port status mismatch), resync that resource first

admin_api_servers_rescue.usage_note: Boot a server into rescue mode (a temporary recovery image with the original disk attached) -- for repairing an unbootable guest.

admin_api_servers_reset_state.usage_note: Force a server's status field back to a known value in the database, without touching the actual hypervisor/guest state. A last-resort admin override for a stuck status, not a fix for whatever caused the stuck state -- confirm the real state first (console-log/action-log) before overriding what's recorded.

admin_api_servers_resize.usage_note: Resize a server to a different flavor/type. Disruptive -- typically involves a reboot and a resize-confirm step depending on the backend.

admin_api_servers_unrescue.usage_note: Exit rescue mode and boot the server normally again.

admin_api_servers_update_bandwidth.usage_note: Change a server's network bandwidth allocation/limit.

admin_api_servers_update_security_group.usage_note: Change which security group(s) a server belongs to.

admin_api_servers_list_server_status.usage_note: Lighter-weight status-only listing across servers, with the same filter set as admin_api_servers_list -- use when you only need status/power_state, not full server records.

admin_api_servers_update_server_status.usage_note: Bulk status override with no path id -- affects servers matched by the request body, not a single server. Broad blast radius; confirm the request body's scope carefully before calling.
